gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a parking-ready front-and-rear setup costs today with the maker's hardwire kit priced in (VIOFO HK4 $17.99, 70mai UP03 $27.99, Vantrue $29.99), nor that 70mai sells a complete A810S front + rear + card + hardwire kit for $177.78 while VIOFO's own store has the A229 Plus 2CH at $229.99, over the $200 line.
standout_why: Compared against knowledgelib.io (cited), dashcamtalk.com (cited), pcworld.com (cited) and productbible.com; vortexradar.com (cited) and winchinsider.com returned HTTP 403, and thecargearguide.com failed on a certificate error, so those three were not read. knowledgelib already says VIOFO's store had the A229 Plus 2CH at $229.99 (dated 2026-10-14) and that it is under $200 only at Amazon, so that part is not new; it gives no price for the HK4 or any other hardwire kit. DashCamTalk, PCWorld and Product Bible give no hardwire kit price and no camera + kit + card total. ChatGPT's own answer flags the question ('if your $200 limit includes all accessories, that matters') and leaves it unanswered. None of the pages read mentions DDPAI or a camera with built-in storage.
decides: It qualifies the pick but does not overturn it. The VIOFO A229 Plus 2CH (1440p front + 1440p rear, IMX675 on both) is under $200 only at a third-party retailer: VIOFO's own US store has it at $229.99 today, and I could not open a Best Buy or Amazon price myself. For a shopper whose $200 must cover parking mode and a card, the 70mai A810S Road Trip Kit at $177.78 is the complete setup under the line from a maker's store. Our row that belongs on the question's own terms is the DDPAI N5 Pro: 4K front + 1440p rear with 64 GB built in, so no card to buy, at {after:ddpai-n5-pro}; that holds only if its store price is re-confirmed (see the DDPAI finding and unsourced). The Botslab G980H 4-camera is also under $200 through our link and includes a rear camera, as the 4-channel option.
